past.words:
HOW WE DIFFER

Longer is not always stronger.

The sector has learnt that a long lease alone cannot make supported housing sustainable. It also takes evidence, clear accountability and the freedom to respond when circumstances change.

CHOOSE A CHAPTER

01

What failed

THE LESSONS LEARNT
What we learnt
03
OUR SUSTAINABLE SOLUTION
What we built

THE PAST FAILURES

Long leases were treated as proof of security.

Long commitments could outlast the demand, funding and working assumptions behind them. When circumstances changed, there was little room to respond.

Homes secured before local demand was properly evidenced
Housing, care and asset management working separately
Risk carried forward instead of reviewed as conditions changed

FIXED

ONE LONG TERM, NO REVIEW POINT

One long fixed term · the legacy model
5 years+ · FRI or internal repairing · CPI-linked · renewable

Agility

We can respond when commissioning, funding or local demand changes.

Risk mitigation

We review the evidence and performance before carrying risk forward.

Long-term resilience

Each renewal is a fresh, informed decision—not an assumption made decades earlier.



Updated 2 June 2026

THE LESSONS LEARNT

A lease only works when the model around it works.

Local need, public funding, regulation and people's circumstances all change. A sustainable model needs regular reviews and shared responsibility.

Start with evidence of need, not simply an available property
Keep the investor, leaseholder, provider and care team connected
Review the model regularly instead of relying on old assumptions

OUR SUSTAINABLE SOLUTION

Five-year-plus leases, renewed on evidence.

Our leases run for five years or more on full repairing and insuring or internal repairing terms, with CPI-linked rent and renewal at the end of the term: a clear point to review demand, funding and policy while residents keep the stability of their home.

Full repairing and insuring (FRI) or internal repairing terms
Rent linked to CPI for the life of the lease
Renewal at the end of the term, decided on the evidence of demand
